summary.text: Kristian Carranza is the Democratic candidate for Texas House of Representatives District 118 in the November 3, 2026, general election, where Republican Jorge Borrego is also on the ballot in a race with no incumbent.
Carranza also ran for the seat in 2024.

paragraphs.text: Carranza advanced from the Democratic primary for District 118 on March 3, 2026, receiving 13,331 votes in a race with no other Democrat on the ballot.
In 2024, Carranza defeated Carlos Quezada in the Democratic primary, 63.1% to 36.9%, and then lost the general election to Republican incumbent John Lujan, 48.3% to 51.7%.

In a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey completed in 2023, Carranza said that work began at age 16 and that, after returning home during senior year at A&M Corpus Christi to support family, a return to school was followed by jobs as a community organizer, work on campaigns across the country, and management of staff and million-dollar budgets, including time in Washington, D.C., and at the White House.

Carranza listed three key messages in that survey: supporting public schools and teacher pay, standing up for every woman's right to make her own healthcare choices, and affordable healthcare for all Texans.
